A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CachePrune study despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be reliably matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original CachePrune experiments on SQuAD, HotpotQA, and WildChat, including ablations, transfer tests, and adaptive attacks.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices, including Tables 1–14.

M1.justification: The attribution scoring, maximum aggregation, subset Φ, pruning mask, preferential loss, and trigger-token procedure are retained. Describing pruning as occurring during KV-cache encoding clarifies the existing procedure without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same QA and dialogue-summarization coverage, code/text injection tasks, four attack-instruction types, and adaptive-attack scenarios. Renumbered appendices retain the existing experiments.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain Vanilla, Delimiting, Datamarking, Sandwich, and Encode_Base64. Adaptive-attack comparisons retain Vanilla, Delimiting, and Datamarking. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The model configurations, dataset splits, metrics, and default N=8, p=0.5%, k=1, and α=1 settings remain unchanged. The adaptive-attack token counts, training budgets, transfer procedures, and judging prompts are also retained.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same pruning-ratio, trigger-token, intervention-strength, subset-Φ, and sample-count analyses, alongside attack transfer and adaptive-attack tests. Moving Table 3 and the layer-distribution plot into the main text adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both report three trials and retain the same plus/minus reporting for CachePrune results. No additional run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: All fourteen tables retain their matched result entries and numerical values, and the experimental plots are reused. For example, CachePrune's Llama3-8B SQuAD ASR remains 7.44±0.22 in Table 1.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, Lemma 1, and their proofs in Appendices B–D are retained. Equation 4 explicitly states the already specified context-token range; other equation edits simplify notation. The relocated DPO explanation introduces no new derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain efficient, sample-efficient KV-cache pruning that reduces injection success while preserving user-task performance. The DPO connection gains prominence in the abstract but was already presented in v2's introduction and Appendix B.

C2.justification: Section 2.4 adds a noise-based explanation for using only initial response tokens. Section 4.2 replaces the model-specific key/value interpretation with an account involving attention routing and preservation of contextual content. Section 2.2.2 explicitly discusses the intervention-strength tradeoff; the stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly discloses ChatGPT assistance with code development and writing refinement. This adds limited information about the development process; existing implementation settings, evaluation code listings, and judging prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to DRIP, Li and Fung's security survey, and Geva et al. It removes Syed et al. and Wu et al.'s attribution/intervention discussion, including the explicit qualification that a completely new intervention technique is not claimed. Several detection-work references are metadata updates to already cited titles.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method exposition, and discussion undergo extensive rewriting. The DPO simplification rationale moves into Appendix B, while the former sampling appendix is folded into Figure 7's caption. These changes substantially revise the exposition despite stable scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with icons and revised labels. The former appendix Figure 6 becomes main-text Figure 4, the pruning-ratio plot becomes Figure 6, and Table 3 moves into the main text. These are targeted display and placement changes within the retained overall format.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity through more direct explanations of attribution and clean-response preservation, while bringing existing supporting evidence closer to the main analysis. The experimental and theoretical substance remains intact. Removing the attribution-patching discussion weakens research positioning, but the overall readability and organization gains support a limited improvement.
